message.content:
Based on my search, here is a comprehensive overview of BMI standards:

## Standard BMI Classification (WHO/CDC - General Adult Population)

The most widely used BMI classification system for adults (ages 18-64) is:

| Category | BMI Range (kg/m²) |
|----------|-------------------|
| Underweight | Below 18.5 |
| Normal/Healthy weight | 18.5 – 24.9 |
| Overweight | 25.0 – 29.9 |
| Obesity Class I | 30.0 – 34.9 |
| Obesity Class II | 35.0 – 39.9 |
| Obesity Class III | 40.0 and above |

## Asian-Specific BMI Standards

Research shows that Asian populations develop metabolic diseases at lower BMI values than Western populations due to higher visceral fat at equivalent BMIs. The WHO recommends **lower thresholds for Asian adults**:

| Category | BMI Range (kg/m²) |
|----------|-------------------|
| Underweight | Below 18.5 |
| Normal weight | 18.5 – 22.9 |
| Overweight | 23.0 – 27.4 |
| Obese | 27.5 and above |

## China's BMI Standards

According to the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention (China CDC):
- **Normal BMI range**: 18.5 to 23.9
- **Overweight**: BMI ≥ 24
- **Obesity**: BMI ≥ 28
- People over 65 can have a slightly higher body weight and BMI

## Recent Updates and Important Considerations (2025-2026)

1. **BMI alone is no longer considered sufficient** - The Lancet Commission and CDC now recommend using BMI alongside at least one other measurement such as:
   - Waist circumference
   - Waist-to-hip ratio
   - Waist-to-height ratio
   - Body fat percentage

2. **Age-specific adjustments for older adults (65+)**:
   - A BMI of **23-28** is associated with lower mortality risk for seniors
   - Standard adult categories may overestimate risk in this group

3. **Waist circumference thresholds**:
   - General adults: Men >40 inches (102 cm), Women >35 inches (89 cm) indicates elevated risk
   - Asian populations: Men >90 cm, Women >80 cm

4. **New obesity definition framework (2025)**: Some experts now propose defining obesity based on:
   - Elevated BMI plus elevated anthropometric measure, OR
   - BMI >40, OR
   - At least 2 elevated anthropometric measures, OR
   - Excess body fat measured by DXA or similar

## BMI Formula

BMI = weight (kg) ÷ height² (m²)

## Limitations of BMI

BMI does not distinguish between muscle and fat, so it may misclassify:
- Athletes and muscular individuals (may read as overweight/obese despite low body fat)
- Pregnant women
- Elderly with sarcopenia (age-related muscle loss)

7. https://bmicalculatorweb.com/blog/cdc-bmi-guidelines-updates.html
8. https://bmicalculatorweb.com/blog/bmi-research-guidelines-updates-latest-findings.html
